title: MS Dhoni ends IPL playing career and becomes Chennai mentor
excerpt: Five titles and 278 matches later, MS Dhoni has retired from the IPL and will guide Chennai Super Kings as team mentor from 2027.
content_html:
MS Dhoni has played his last match in the Indian Premier League. Chennai Super Kings announced on 17 November that their long-time captain will retire as a player and become team mentor from the 2027 season.

The decision came from Dhoni himself. Chennai owner Rupa Gurunath said he asked for his name to go on the club's release list during a video call on 14 November, when management was discussing retentions.

The record

Dhoni finishes with 5,439 runs in 278 IPL matches, including 24 half-centuries. For Chennai he made 272 appearances, more than any other player, and scored 5,314 runs, the second-most in the club's history.

His captaincy record is the bigger legacy:

  • Five IPL titles, in 2010, 2011, 2018, 2021 and 2023, equal to Rohit Sharma's record at Mumbai Indians
  • Ten IPL finals with Chennai
  • Play-off appearances in 12 seasons
  • Champions League T20 titles in 2010 and 2014

Chennai bought Dhoni at the first IPL auction in 2008 and made him captain from the start. The only break came in 2016 and 2017, when Chennai were suspended and he played for Rising Pune Supergiant.

A quiet ending

For a player known for last-over finishes, the end was low-key. Dhoni, 45, missed the whole 2026 season with injury. Chennai finished eighth and missed the play-offs for the third year in a row.

He retired from international cricket in August 2020 but played on for Chennai for another six seasons.

His win rate of 57.87 per cent is the best of any IPL captain to have led in more than 60 matches. He captained Chennai 221 times between 2008 and 2025.

Chennai managing director KS Viswanathan said Dhoni had embraced the city, and the city had embraced him as one of its own.

Chennai chairman N Srinivasan said there was no CSK without Dhoni and that the franchise would always be his home.

What's next for Chennai

The club now has to rebuild without the player many fans see as the franchise itself. Keeping Dhoni involved as mentor offers some continuity, starting at next month's mini-auction in Goa on 16 December.
